title: ViewSwitcher
summary: Switches one data set between views such as table, board and calendar: Material 3 segmented buttons with an icon and a label per view.
whenToUse: Above a collection that can be shown in two to four layouts, where the choice changes how the same records are drawn.
whenNotToUse: For filters that change which records are shown, use chips or a filter bar. For five or more views, or a narrow screen where the labels do not fit, use an exposed dropdown menu.
api: SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow { views.forEachIndexed { index, view -> SegmentedButton(selected = index == selected, onClick = { selected = index }, shape = SegmentedButtonDefaults.itemShape(index, views.size), icon = { MonarchIcon(view.icon, contentDescription = null, size = MonarchIconSize.Sm) }, label = { Text(view.label) }) } }

options.name: selected
options.description: Whether the segment is the current view; hoisted in the app.

options.name: icon
options.description: The icon of the view, a MonarchIcon with a null content description. The default draws a check mark on the selected segment.

options.name: label
options.description: The name of the view, with a count after it when it helps: "Board 12".

states.name: selected
states.description: The segment takes the selected colors of the theme mapping and the selected state.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The segment cannot be chosen and takes the disabled colors.

appearance: A MonarchSegmentedControl: a muted track with a raised pill under the chosen view, a 16dp icon before each label in the content color of the segment. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ViewSwitcher is a component with built-in labels and icons for table, board, calendar, gallery, list and timeline, counts, sizes and labels that hide on narrow screens. On Android MonarchSegmentedControl switches between views with the radio roles of the platform, so Monarch ships no separate component: the app supplies the names and the icons (Monarch bundles none), so there are no built-in strings. A segment shows the icon and the label together; when four labels do not fit at a large font size, use fewer views or an exposed dropdown menu instead of hiding the labels. iOS shares the recipe approach with a segmented Picker.
accessibility: Each segment is a selectable element in a group; TalkBack reads its label and "selected".
The icons have a null content description, so the label is the name.
Each segment has a 48dp touch target from Material 3.
edgeCases: Long labels wrap inside the segment at large font sizes; keep labels to one word.
Keep the chosen view in saveable state or the view model so it survives a configuration change.

examples.title: Default views
examples.template:
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3)) {
MonarchSegmentedControl {
    Segment(
        selected = mode == {{views.0.value}},
        onClick = { mode = {{views.0.value}} },
        label = {{views.0.label}},
        icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.Table, contentDescription = null, size = MonarchIconSize.Sm) },
    )
    Segment(
        selected = mode == {{views.1.value}},
        onClick = { mode = {{views.1.value}} },
        label = {{views.1.label}},
        icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.Board, contentDescription = null, size = MonarchIconSize.Sm) },
    )
    Segment(
        selected = mode == {{views.2.value}},
        onClick = { mode = {{views.2.value}} },
        label = {{views.2.label}},
        icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.CalendarMonth, contentDescription = null, size = MonarchIconSize.Sm) },
    )
    Segment(
        selected = mode == {{views.3.value}},
        onClick = { mode = {{views.3.value}} },
        label = {{views.3.label}},
        icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.Grid, contentDescription = null, size = MonarchIconSize.Sm) },
    )
}
MonarchText(text = "Showing the $mode view.", style = MonarchTextStyle.Caption)
}

parityExceptions.reason: Four segments with an icon and a label each (Table, Board, Calendar, Gallery) need about 430dp on one line, as on the web. A phone window is 344dp wide, where the control wraps or cuts a label, so the docs preview is recorded in a tablet window (840dp) where the segments sit on one line.
parityExceptions.convention: a segmented control keeps every label whole on one line (Material segmented button); it is shown at the width it needs
